hinweis: Ding · Herkunft · Haken, nie wer es liebt. Die Wirkung (Bonus, Heilung) bleibt als eigene Zeile und steht hier nicht. OK / Ändern + Notiz.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Golden, still warm, wrapped in greaseproof paper. The village bakery makes exactly twelve a morning. By nine, there are none.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Green-gold, bottled by hand with a paper label. The groves above Cala d'Orsu are older than the church. Some families still argue about which tree is theirs.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A jar of salt, chilli and something that sparkles. Lola won't say what. It goes on everything, and everything is better for it.

items.feld: Tim Tams from Alva's Bar · wholesome
items.alt: The only Australian biscuits in all of Corsica. Lola cries a little.
items.neu: Chocolate biscuits from the other side of the world, in a packet slightly crushed by the journey. Nobody in Corsica knows how Alva gets them.

items.feld: A Plate of Lola's Biscuits · wholesome
items.alt: Megan doesn't eat sugar. Except these.
items.neu: Buttery, uneven, a little burnt at one edge. Lola bakes them at three in the morning when she can't sleep. Even people who swear off sugar don't say no.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Purple figs, split open by the sun. Alva buys them from a woman who won't sell to anyone she doesn't like.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Forty grams of protein and the taste of cardboard with ambition. Totò keeps a box of them for the gym people. He won't eat one himself.

items.alt: Like in Hamburg. Almost. Lola helped.
items.neu: Flattened, sticky with cinnamon, folded the way they do it up north. Lola helped. You can tell, because there's a little glitter in it.

items.alt: Corsican biscuits that keep forever.
items.neu: Hard Corsican biscuits that taste of aniseed and keep for months. Fishermen took them out to sea when the bread would have gone soft.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Dark as a bruise and twice as sweet. Every family in Cala d'Orsu swears theirs is the original recipe. Alva keeps hers under the counter, next to the diesel.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Peat smoke in a bottle, from a cold island far to the north. It costs more than Totò's monthly rent. He says the case fell off a very expensive boat.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Bright yellow, ice cold, made in someone's kitchen. Alva doesn't sell the recipe. She does sell the bottle, and the bottle is enough.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A bitter Corsican aperitif with quinine and orange peel. The old men at the harbour drink it at six, every day, as if the clock depended on it.

items.feld: Pink Pearl on a Fine Chain · wholesome
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A single pink pearl on a chain as fine as a hair. Totò wrapped it in tissue paper, which is how you know he didn't steal this one.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A faceted bottle with a heavy gold cap. Smells of money, cold rooms and someone who always gets the last word.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Tiny white shells threaded on a silver chain. Alva says the village girls wear them until they marry, and then never take them off.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Enormous heart-shaped sunglasses with rhinestones on the corners. Subtle as a brass band. Somebody in Cala d'Orsu will wear these with total dignity.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Heavy enough to anchor a dinghy. Totò swears it's real. Totò also swore the goat was a gift.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Black lenses, a logo you can read from the other end of the harbour. Totò calls them “original”. He does not say original what.

items.feld: Slim Silver Ring from the Market · wholesome
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A slim silver band from the Saturday market. Nothing engraved, nothing promised. Just a ring that fits.

items.feld: Belly Button Piercing with a Shell · frech
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A little silver bar with a white shell dangling from it. Alva keeps it in a dish by the till, next to the matches, for the kind of customer who asks.

items.feld: Homemade Shell Necklace with Beads · wholesome
items.alt: Made by the village children, a little crooked. Siri puts it on straight away.
items.neu: Shells and plastic beads on a fishing line, knotted by small hands. One shell is upside down. Nobody would fix it for the world.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Navy blue, embroidered with a golden anchor. Megan's office ships them by the hundred. Nobody in the fleet has ever been seen wearing one.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A glitter sash that reads “Miss Cala d'Orsu”. The village crowned its last Miss in 1987. The sash has been waiting ever since.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A black lace fan from Sevilla, painted with red carnations. It snaps open like a slap. Someone once danced with it until the floor gave up.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Grey wool, a plain Nordic pattern, one heel knitted a little thicker than the other. Whoever made them was counting on cold nights at sea.

items.feld: Wool Hat with a Nordic Pattern · wholesome
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A thick wool hat with a snowflake pattern, completely wrong for Corsica. Alva ordered it for a Norwegian guest years ago. He never came back for it.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Three candles that smell of the hills: myrtle, rosemary and warm stone. Light one and the cabin turns into the maquis at dusk.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A paper bag of glitter confetti, enough for a wedding or a small war. Whoever opens it will be finding it in their hair for weeks.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A string of tiny solar lights in glass drops. Charge them in the sun on deck, and at night the railing looks like it's holding stars.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Chrome, precise to the newton metre, in a case that clicks like a safe. A tool for people who think “tight enough” is a moral failing.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Yellow, rubber-armoured, bright enough to turn the night sea green. Whoever owned it before scratched a small fish into the handle.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A dented aluminium moka pot, the eight-sided kind from Naples. It hisses, it spits, and it makes coffee nobody on this boat can argue with.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Carbon fibre, telescopic, with a remote shutter. It folds down to the size of a pen and opens up to the size of an ego.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Plain polarised sunglasses, the kind that let you see straight through the glare into the water. Coast guards wear them. So do smugglers.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A red pocket knife with nine tools and a toothpick nobody uses. Alva sells exactly one a summer, always to a tourist who swears it's for camping.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Black lacquer, a gold nib, a cap that closes with a soft click. A pen like this doesn't sign receipts. It signs things that matter.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Brown leather with an elastic band, every page still empty. The kind of notebook you buy for the person you want to become.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A second-hand book of poems, the spine cracked open at one page. Someone underlined a single line in pencil, then tried to rub it out.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Tide tables, star charts and sunrise times, bound in dark blue cloth. Sailors who still trust paper over satellites keep one by their bunk.

items.feld: Old Chart of the West Coast · ernst/Lore
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A yellowed chart of the west coast, the rocks drawn by hand. Some of the soundings are wrong now. The sea has moved, the chart hasn't.

items.feld: Duc's Poem about the Sea · wholesome
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A folded page in your own handwriting, crossed out twice and started again. It is not a good poem. It is an honest one.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A second-hand ukulele with a sticker of a pineapple and one string slightly out of tune. It cannot play a sad song. Believe us, people have tried.

items.feld: Men's Magazine with a Pin-Up · frech
items.alt: An Italian magazine with a beautiful, half-naked woman on the cover. Totò reads it “for the articles”.
items.neu: An Italian men's magazine from the eighties, the cover a little sun-bleached. Totò claims he only reads it for the interviews.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A spiral shell, cream outside and pink inside, the kind children press to their ear. If you listen, the sea is still in there.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A piece of green bottle glass, worn smooth and cloudy by years of waves. Somebody's broken bottle became somebody else's treasure.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A single red rose from the vase on Alva's bar. She never gives the roses away. She gave you one.

items.alt: Rusty, fished out of the bay.
items.neu: A small brass anchor on a keyring, green with salt, fished out of the bay. Whatever keys it once held are still somewhere at the bottom.

items.alt: Wild myrtle and rosemary from the hillside.
items.neu: Wild myrtle, rosemary and a sprig of something yellow nobody can name. Picked on the hillside, it smells of the whole island at once.

items.feld: Small Branch of Coral (Beach Find) · ernst/Lore
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A small branch of red coral, washed up after a storm. The old fishermen say coral keeps you from drowning. The old fishermen also say a lot of things.

items.feld: Goldfish in a Water Bag · witzig
items.alt: From a stall at the Festa. Lea names it immediately, somehow.
items.neu: A small orange fish in a plastic bag of water, won at the Festa. It looks at you as if this was entirely your idea.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Neroli and sweet almond in a dark glass bottle. Warm it in your hands first. That's not a tip, that's a promise.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Midnight silk, lined so nothing gets through. Totò hands it over without a single word, which for Totò is a first.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Black silk with red cranes, light enough to fall off a shoulder by accident. Accidents like that are the whole point.

items.feld: Massage Candle with Warming Oil · frech
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A candle that melts into warm oil. Alva wraps it in brown paper and doesn't ask questions, which is its own kind of question.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Sheer black stockings with a lace top that stays up on its own. Totò files them under “luxury textiles”, between the towels and the tablecloths.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Four satin ribbons with soft cuffs, made to fit any bed. Totò's note says “for tying up loose ends”. He's very proud of that one.

items.feld: Nipple Clamps with a Chain · frech
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Two little clamps on a fine silver chain, adjustable, as the box assures you three times. Totò pretends it's jewellery. It sort of is.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Champagne-coloured lace, more air than fabric. It came in a box with a ribbon, and the ribbon was the least of it.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Pink fluffy handcuffs with a tiny key. The fluff is for comfort. The key, Totò says, is optional.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Smooth, quiet, waterproof, in Eden blue with a tiny gold anchor. Nobody at the Eden Group will admit who signed off on the merchandise.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Polished steel with a sparkling pink stone on the end. Totò holds the box at arm's length and says, “Very elegant. Very discreet.” It is neither.

items.alt: Red and black, from Alva's own stock under the counter.
items.neu: Red and black, with ruffles that move like a skirt in the wind. Alva keeps it under the counter, and it isn't for sale to just anyone.

items.feld: A Cup Just for Her · wholesome
items.alt: Hand-painted in Petru's workshop, with her name on it. For her, not for the guests. Chain: Petru + Lola.
items.neu: A cup painted by hand in Petru's workshop, her name on the side in careful letters. Not a guest cup. Hers.

items.alt: Carved from driftwood by Petru. For the workshop she wants to have one day.
items.neu: Driftwood, carved letters: “Scuderi & Figlie”. A sign for a workshop that doesn't exist yet. Petru carved it as if it already does.

items.feld: A Pen with Her Own Name · ernst/Lore
items.alt: Engraved with Sophia Moore, not with any other name. For what she wants to write herself.
items.neu: A pen engraved with Sophia Moore, and no other name. For the first thing she writes that is hers.

items.alt: For her own plans, safely planned. Chain: Elsa + Totò.
items.neu: A dive computer, tested and set to her depths. For the dives she plans herself, and comes back from.

items.feld: Guide: The Art of Fishing in Corsica · wholesome
items.alt: From Petru's stories, bound by hand. For her father.
items.neu: Petru's stories about fishing the Corsican coast, bound by hand in linen. A book for a father who used to take his daughter out on the water.

items.alt: From Alva's secret stash. Lola calls it home in brown.
items.neu: A jar of black-brown spread from Alva's secret stash. The rest of Europe calls it a mistake. Some people call it home.

items.alt: Repaired by Petru. Chain: Alva + Petru.
items.neu: Her grandmother's castanets from Sevilla, broken for years, mended by Petru so they click again. Some things wait a long time to be played.

items.feld: A Card Signed by the Whole Crew · wholesome
items.alt: Framed. None of it can be bought.
items.neu: A card in a plain frame, signed by every single person on the boat. You can buy a yacht. You can't buy this.

items.feld: A Tin of Norwegian Salt Liquorice · witzig
items.alt: Bring-me job: Elsa takes it to the hospital.
items.neu: A tin of Norwegian salt liquorice, black and fierce. Most people spit it out. The people who don't are usually from very cold places.

items.feld: San Gennaro Figurine from Naples · wholesome
items.alt: Chain: the cousin from Bastia + Alva.
items.neu: A painted plaster San Gennaro from a stall in Naples, a little chipped at the halo. Every Neapolitan kitchen has one watching over the coffee.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Gold-framed sunglasses with “Monaco” on the arm in tiny letters. They make any face look like it owns a boat, which is the point.

items.alt: With her initials. She laughs out loud for the first time.
items.neu: A ticket book bound in leather, her initials pressed into the cover. Finally, something worthy of her handwriting.

items.alt: Bring-me job: only Totò can get it.
items.neu: Dark pipe tobacco from Bastia, the kind they stopped selling in the village years ago. It smells of a wheelhouse at night.

items.alt: For the Festa. She will aim it at the yacht.
items.neu: A confetti cannon as big as a small car, with a crank. Officially for the Festa. Unofficially, it will be pointed at the yacht.

items.alt: At the farewell, from Holm's trust 2. Her father's compass.
items.neu: Brass, scratched glass, a needle that still finds north. It belonged to Holm's father. She gave it to you at the gangway, without a speech.

items.alt: +1 Courage while you carry it.
items.neu: A small hammer with a handle worn dark by one man's grip. Petru fixes boats with it. Lent to you, it feels like a vote of confidence.

items.alt: +1 Perception while you carry it.
items.neu: An old dive mask with a cracked strap, mended with tape. Lea saw her first reef through it. She swears it still remembers the way.

items.alt: +1 Perception while you carry it.
items.neu: A heavy black service torch from the Gendarmerie Maritime. It has found smugglers, lost dogs and one very embarrassed mayor.

items.alt: +1 Cunning while you carry it.
items.neu: Leather workshop gloves, oil-black, a hole in the left thumb. Rosi says the hole is a design feature.

items.alt: +1 Cunning while you carry it.
items.neu: A greasy little notebook full of prices, nicknames and debts in Totò's code. Half of the island is in here. Some of them owe him a goat.

items.alt: +1 Charm while you carry it.
items.neu: A silk neckerchief, sea-blue, that still smells faintly of her perfume. She wore it on a shoot once and said it was the only real thing in the picture.

items.alt: Black onyx, a golden anchor. From Megan's trust 3 in the Eden Shop.
items.neu: Black onyx cufflinks with a small golden anchor. Fleet issue for directors only. Megan doesn't give them away. She lends them, which is worse.

items.alt: +1 Empathy while you carry it.
items.neu: A woven friendship bracelet in all the colours of the galley. Lola made two. She's wearing the other one.

items.alt: +1 Empathy while you carry it.
items.neu: A thin silver bookmark, cool to the touch, slipped between two pages for you to find. She marked the place where she stopped reading. Or started.

items.alt: Once a day, advantage on Cunning.
items.neu: A well-worn stainless multitool with eleven functions and one that nobody has ever figured out. Alva swears it opened a bottle of wine during the storm of '09.

items.alt: Once a day, advantage on Cunning.
items.neu: A slim leather wallet of picks and tension wrenches. Totò says they're for “emergencies”. He has a lot of emergencies.

items.alt: Once a day, advantage on Perception.
items.neu: Heavy naval binoculars with a cracked leather strap. Someone in the village watched every ship come and go through these for thirty years.

items.alt: Once a day, advantage on Perception.
items.neu: Petru's old fishing knife, the blade thin from sharpening. It has gutted more fish than you'll eat in your life. He gave it without looking up.

items.alt: Once a day, advantage on Charm.
items.neu: Aftershave “Bastia”: cedar, lime and the confidence of a man with a gold tooth. Alva sells it to sailors who want to be remembered.

items.alt: Once a day, advantage on Charm.
items.neu: A purple plectrum with a tiny bite mark. Lola plays with it when she thinks nobody is listening. Everybody is listening.

items.alt: She says it was a mistake. Megan McAllister doesn't make mistakes. Once a day: advantage on Charm with Megan.
items.neu: She says it was a mistake. Megan McAllister doesn't make mistakes.

items.alt: Once a day, advantage on Courage.
items.neu: An old ten-franc coin, worn smooth on one side. Alva's father kept it in the till for forty years. She doesn't say why she's giving it to you.

items.feld: Badge of the Gendarmerie Maritime · ernst/Lore
items.alt: Once a day, advantage on Courage.
items.neu: The badge of the Gendarmerie Maritime, enamel chipped at one corner. People stand differently when they see it. So, it turns out, do you.

items.alt: A little silver hand on a black cord. Mazzere wear it so they wake up from the hunt.
items.neu: A little silver hand on a black cord. Mazzere wear it so they wake up from the hunt.

items.alt: A white képi with a frayed band. People stand up straighter when they see it.
items.neu: A white képi with a frayed band. People stand up straighter when they see it.

items.alt: Once a day, advantage on Empathy.
items.neu: A worn deck of tarot cards, the edges soft as cloth. One card is missing. Whoever took it knew exactly which one.

items.alt: Once a day, advantage on Empathy.
items.neu: A single knot cut out of one of Petru's nets, tight and neat as a heartbeat. He says a good knot holds without being pulled.

items.alt: At Alva's, one can a day at most, and dearer than at Totò's.
items.neu: A red jerry can, dented, smelling of the harbour. Alva's is dearer than Totò's. Alva's also didn't fall off anything.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Scratched, dented, still holding a charge. Mostly out of spite.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A spray bottle of solar panel cleaner and a squeegee. Glamorous it isn't. Neither is a dead battery at two in the morning.

items.alt: Screws, seals, cable lugs. Rosi beams.
items.neu: A box of screws, seals and cable lugs, sorted by nobody. To most people it's junk. To Rosi it's Christmas.

items.alt: In a fight: +3 stamina, but your hands shake: parry window −10 % this round. Quick: costs no turn.
items.neu: A double espresso in a paper cup, strong enough to restart a heart. Your hands will thank you later. Not now.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Oats, dates, honey and a pinch of salt, wrapped in baking paper with a smiley drawn on it. Lola makes a batch every Monday.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A jar of very green pesto with a handwritten label: “SPECIAL”. Lola winks when she hands it over. Do not ask what makes it special.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Today's catch on a bed of ice, eyes still bright. It was in the sea this morning. By tonight, it'll be dinner.

items.feld: Ice Packs from the Village · witzig
items.alt: The supplies last a day longer when power runs low.
items.neu: Blue ice packs from the village shop. In a heatwave with no power, they are worth more than gold. Gold doesn't keep the butter cold.

items.alt: From Madame Casanova's hair, after the flamenco. Used once: Desire +6 with every woman.
items.neu: A red rose from Madame Casanova's hair, thrown after the flamenco. Every woman on the boat saw where it landed.

items.feld: Spare Cells for the House Battery · witzig
items.alt: Two lithium cells, used, tested.
items.neu: Two used lithium cells, tested, labelled in marker: “PROBABLY FINE”. That's Totò's highest grade of quality.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A compressor relay the size of a matchbox. Without it, the cold room is just a room. With it, the crew eats tomorrow.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A handful of brass letters, polished by Totò's sleeve. Enough to spell a name, if you choose carefully.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A pot of bone glue, the old kind that has to be warmed. It smells terrible. It holds forever. Petru won't use anything else.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: An old oak board, dark with age, from a door that no longer exists. Alva had it in the back room. She said it was too good to burn.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A sack of grey clay from the riverbank. Cold, heavy, and ready to become anything, if someone patient gets their hands on it.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A button cell for a watch, sealed in plastic you can't open without a knife and swearing.

items.feld: Gold Paint and a Fine Brush · wholesome
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A little tin of gold paint and a brush with three hairs. For the details nobody notices until they're missing.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A few threads of real saffron in a twist of paper, worth more than their weight in silver. Alva keeps it in the till, not the kitchen.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A roll of bookbinding linen in faded blue. Stories need covers, too, or they fall apart.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A roll of tarred net twine. Every fisherman in the bay has mended a net with this, and every one of them has a theory about the right knot.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A plain wooden frame, nothing fancy. It doesn't need to be. What goes inside is the point.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A silicone strap, fleet grey. Totò says it fell off a container in Livorno. Very gently.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A pen blank, smooth, waiting to be engraved. Right now it's nobody's pen. Soon it'll be somebody's.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Seawater-proof antenna cable, a whole coil. Officially for the gendarmerie. Unofficially, don't ask Totò where he got it.

items.alt: Advantage on repair jobs (or +2 if your craft already gives advantage).
items.neu: A battered red toolbox with a dent in the lid and everything in its place. Someone loved these tools before you did.

items.alt: Advantage on cooking jobs (or +2 if your cooking already gives advantage).
items.neu: A Japanese chef's knife, the steel folded until it shows a pattern like water. It doesn't cut so much as agree with the onion.

items.alt: In a fight: heals 10 % of your HP and stops bleeding. Quick: costs no turn.
items.neu: A box of plasters with cartoon dolphins on them. They work just as well as the boring ones, and they look better on a hero.

items.alt: In a fight: heals 25 % of your HP and stops bleeding.
items.neu: A rolled bandage, still sealed. Every boat has a drawer of these. Every captain hopes they stay in it.

items.alt: In a fight: heals 40 % of your HP and stops bleeding and burning.
items.neu: A green first aid kit with the Eden anchor on the lid. Somebody has written “USE ME” on it in red marker. Somebody has clearly needed to.

items.alt: In a fight: puts out every flame on you, and you can't catch fire for 2 rounds. Quick: costs no turn.
items.neu: A can of cooling spray meant for sprained ankles. Turns out it does wonders for being on fire.

items.alt: In a fight: their next attack hits only smoke, and next turn you can run without a roll (not from bosses).
items.neu: A tin smoke pot, the kind used to signal from lifeboats. Pull the ring and the world turns grey for a while.

items.alt: Isabelle's remedy from the monastery pharmacy. In a fight: ends every bad state on you.
items.neu: A dark tincture in a corked bottle from the monastery pharmacy. Bitter enough to make your eyes water. That's how you know it works.

items.alt: In a fight: +2 stamina. Quick: costs no turn.
items.neu: A single espresso. Small, black, and deeply judgemental.

items.alt: In a fight: +1 stamina every round for 4 rounds. Quick: costs no turn.
items.neu: An espresso with water added, which any Italian on board will tell you is a crime. Still, it keeps you going.

items.alt: In a fight: clears your head of stun and blindness, +1 stamina.
items.neu: Mate in a gourd with a metal straw. Bitter, grassy, and it clears your head faster than a slap.

items.alt: In a fight: parry window +15 % for 3 rounds. Quick: costs no turn.
items.neu: A cup of green tea, steam curling. It doesn't make you faster. It makes everything else slower.

items.alt: In a fight, thrown at an animal: it eats instead of biting, skips a round and loses 4 composure.
items.neu: A tin of dog food with a picture of a very happy labrador. Hungry animals take the deal more often than you'd think.

items.alt: In a fight: a human loses 5 composure, an animal is exhausted for 2 rounds.
items.neu: A white megaphone with the Eden logo. Megan's office sends them out for “crew motivation”. Nobody knows if that's a joke.

items.alt: In a fight: you patch your jacket, protection +2 for the rest of the fight.
items.neu: A roll of silver duct tape. It has held together boats, marriages and at least one rescue helicopter.

items.alt: For sabres: +3 damage for 5 rounds. Use it before a fight or during one.
items.neu: A blue whetstone, wet and smooth. Rosi cut it to fit a sabre. Draw the blade across it slowly, and it starts to sing.

items.alt: For knives: +3 damage for 5 rounds. Use it before a fight or during one.
items.neu: A grey whetstone, small enough for a pocket. For knives that should stay quiet and sharp.

items.alt: For the boar spear: +3 damage for 5 rounds. Use it before a fight or during one.
items.neu: A red whetstone, heavy and coarse, cut for a boar spear. Every stroke takes off a little rust and a little doubt.

items.alt: For blunt weapons: +3 damage for 5 rounds. Use it before a fight or during one.
items.neu: Steel spikes that strap onto anything blunt. Rosi calls it “persuasion hardware”.

items.alt: For the shotgun: +3 damage for 5 rounds. Use it before a fight or during one.
items.neu: Hand-loaded match ammunition, every cartridge weighed. Rosi doesn't trust factory rounds. Rosi doesn't trust factories.

items.alt: One of Rosi's home-made grenades. In a fight: 12 % of the enemy's HP straight through armour, and it burns (2 stacks).
items.neu: One of Rosi's home-made grenades, warm to the touch for no good reason. The label says DO NOT SHAKE. It has been shaken.

items.alt: Rosi filled it from an old fire extinguisher. In a fight: 12 % of the enemy's HP straight through armour, and it's wet.
items.neu: Rosi filled it from an old fire extinguisher and a lot of optimism. It's wet. Spectacularly wet.

items.alt: Two battery cells and a lot of tape. In a fight: 12 % of the enemy's HP straight through armour, and it's charged. On a wet enemy: short circuit.
items.neu: Two battery cells and a lot of tape. Rosi says it's perfectly safe. Rosi also lost her eyebrows once.

items.alt: No damage, just light. In a fight: the enemy is blinded for a round and its next blow does half damage.
items.neu: No damage, just light. For one long second, everything goes white and very quiet.

items.alt: Heavy, and it means it. In a fight: 12 % of the enemy's HP straight through armour, and it's shaken (armour gone).
items.neu: Heavy, and it means it. Rosi drew a little smiley face on it, which is somehow worse.

items.alt: Packed with boat nails. In a fight: 18 % of the enemy's HP straight through armour, and it bleeds. Useless against machines.
items.neu: Packed with boat nails from Rosi's workshop. Useless against machines. Not useless against anything else.

items.alt: A steel plate for Rosi's workshop: the first upgrade for a jacket or Gemelli.
items.neu: A plain steel plate, heavy and honest. Rosi taps it twice, listens, and nods like a doctor.

items.alt: A titanium plate for Rosi's workshop: the second upgrade for a jacket or Gemelli.
items.neu: Black titanium, light for its strength, blue at the edges. Taken from something that was built to win.

items.alt: A stone for Rosi: it replaces Terremoto's base stone (first upgrade).
items.neu: A smooth green jade, cool in the hand. Rosi says stone remembers the ground it came from.

items.alt: A stone for Rosi: it replaces Le Large's base stone (first upgrade).
items.neu: A golden topaz, warm as late sun. It looks like it's been holding a little light all this time.

items.alt: A stone for Rosi: it replaces Riposte's base stone (first upgrade).
items.neu: A pale aquamarine, the colour of the bay at seven in the morning, before the boats come out.

items.alt: A stone for Rosi: it replaces Sussurro's base stone (first upgrade).
items.neu: A violet amethyst. Sailors once wore them against drunkenness. It didn't work, but they kept wearing them.

items.alt: A precious stone for Rosi: Terremoto's final stone (second upgrade).
items.neu: A deep green emerald, flawed inside like a forest. Rosi won't cut it. She says the flaw is where the strength is.

items.alt: A precious stone for Rosi: Le Large's final stone (second upgrade).
items.neu: A blood-red ruby. It glows even in the dark of the workshop, as if it were still deciding something.

items.alt: A precious stone for Rosi: Riposte's final stone (second upgrade).
items.neu: A royal blue sapphire, cold and certain. The kind of stone that ends arguments.

items.alt: A precious stone for Rosi: Sussurro's final stone (second upgrade).
items.neu: A white opal full of small fires, blue, green and pink. Turn it in the light and it never shows the same thing twice.

items.alt: A copper ingot for Rosi: the first upgrade for Gemelli.
items.neu: A copper ingot, orange-red and shiny as a new coin. Rosi polished it with her sleeve. Then she polished it again.

items.alt: A silver ingot for Rosi: the second upgrade for Gemelli.
items.neu: A silver ingot, warm white and heavy. Pure enough that Rosi took off her gloves to hold it.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Iron, heavy, tied to a cork float so it won't sink. Petru doesn't give his key to people. He gives it to people he'd let into his boat.

items.feld: The Mayor's Invitation to the Festa · witzig
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Thick cream card, a red wax seal, a sprig of myrtle. Madame Casanova signed it with three exclamation marks. One would have been a lot.

items.feld: Key to Alva's Back Room · frech
items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: A small brass key on a red ribbon. The back room of Alva's bar has a sofa, a record player and a lock that very few people have seen from the inside.

items.alt: Phone features for one day.
items.neu: A sealed satellite data package with a serial number filed off. Totò calls it “internet from the sky”. The sky did not agree to this.

items.alt: (kein Text)
items.neu: Dark rum with a hand-written label and no tax stamp anywhere. It tastes of molasses, wood and very bad decisions made in very good company.

items.alt: Village Reputation +2 with the old men at the harbour
items.neu: A box of Cohibas, the seal unbroken. The old men at the harbour would sell their grandmothers for one. Some have tried.

items.feld: Crate of Limoncello without a Tax Stamp · witzig
items.alt: to Alva: +240 €
items.neu: Twelve bottles of limoncello, no tax stamp, a crate marked “OLIVES”. The olives are very convincing. Mostly yellow.

items.alt: to Yasin or Casanova: Trust +8
items.neu: Three “designer” handbags, each logo slightly misspelt. From a distance, perfect. From close up, a lot of character.

items.feld: Shell Crown of the Festa · witzig
items.alt: Glitter, shells and dignity.
items.neu: A crown of shells, glitter and hot glue from the Festa. Glitter, shells and dignity, in that order.

items.feld: A Photo You Shouldn't Delete · frech
items.alt: Rosi knows you have it.
items.neu: A photo you were told to delete. Rosi knows you didn't. She hasn't asked. That's the interesting part.

items.alt: “Thank you for my first birthday without a camera.”
items.neu: A small card in neat handwriting: “Thank you for my first birthday without a camera.”

items.feld: Photo of Holm's First Command · ernst/Lore
items.alt: A rusty freighter off Bergen, a young woman in a cap.
items.neu: A rusty freighter off Bergen, a young woman in a cap squinting at the camera. Holm's first command, and she looks like she already knew.

items.alt: She tucked it into your hair while you were dancing.
items.neu: A hairband she tucked into your hair while you were dancing. She laughed when it slipped over one eye. You kept it.

items.alt: A trophy. Megan wants it back. Never.
items.neu: A carbon propeller from Megan's surveillance drone. A trophy. Megan wants it back. Never.

items.alt: A former weapon, later planned as the master weapon for Le Large.
items.neu: A trident of green bronze, crusted with tiny shells, cold even in the sun. It rose from the black pool at high tide. Nobody saw who let go of it.

items.alt: Buttered toast with hundreds and thousands. Lea thinks of birthdays.
items.neu: White toast, butter, and hundreds and thousands of sprinkles. In Australia it means a children's birthday. On this boat it means someone needs cheering up.

items.alt: Chocolate squares rolled in coconut.
items.neu: Squares of sponge cake dipped in chocolate and rolled in coconut. Lola makes them in the exact size of a bad day.

items.feld: Pavlova with Figs and Myrtle · wholesome
items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: A cloud of meringue with cream, fresh figs and a drizzle of myrtle syrup. Australia and Corsica on one plate, and neither of them is complaining.

items.alt: Oat biscuits. Holm's biscuit for every night watch.
items.neu: Oat and golden syrup biscuits that keep for weeks. Soldiers' wives once baked them because they survived the long voyage. Night watches love them for the same reason.

items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: Soft pastry scrolls with cheese and a thin swirl of Vegemite. The Corsicans eye them with suspicion. Then they take a second one.

items.alt: Biscuits and hot cocoa to suck through them.
items.neu: Two chocolate biscuits and a mug of hot cocoa. Bite off the corners, suck the cocoa through, eat fast before it collapses. It always collapses.

items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: Popcorn tossed in Lola's Ocean Glitter spice. It sparkles, it crackles, and it sticks to your fingers like confetti after a parade.

items.alt: Biscuits shaped like seagulls.
items.neu: Shortbread biscuits cut in the shape of seagulls. Bite the heads off first. Kevin is watching. Kevin knows.

items.feld: Red Berry Pudding with Vanilla Sauce · wholesome
items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: Red berry pudding with cold vanilla sauce, the way they make it up north. Lola learned it from a cookbook and a long phone call.

items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: Little shell-shaped cakes with a hint of lavender. Best eaten warm, with tea, and with someone who doesn't need to talk.

items.feld: Cannoli with a Spanner Biscuit · witzig
items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: Crisp Sicilian pastry tubes filled with ricotta, served with a biscuit shaped like a spanner. Lola thinks this is a joke. It is, a little.

items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: A jelly that glows a faint blue in the dark, thanks to tonic water and science. Lola calls it plankton. It is not plankton. Probably.

items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: Crispy seaweed with lime and sea salt, thin as paper. They taste like the first swim of the morning.

items.feld: Protein Pancakes, No Fun Included · witzig
items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: Protein pancakes, no sugar, no butter, no fun included. Lola made them under protest and drew a sad face in the syrup.

items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: Dark chocolate brownies with ghost pepper. The first bite is heaven. The second bite is a war crime.

items.alt: Corsican cheesecake with lemon.
items.neu: Corsican cheesecake made with brocciu and lemon zest, the recipe older than anyone in the village. Lola had to beg for it.

items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: Tiramisu in a cocktail glass, soaked in espresso and coffee liqueur. Dessert and nightcap in one, for people who can't decide.

items.alt: Black, and they taste of vanilla.
items.neu: Pitch-black muffins with a round orange eye of icing. They look like the generator. They taste of vanilla. Unit-01 has not commented.

items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: Mango sorbet with a slow burn of chilli. Sweet first, then trouble. Lola serves it with a wink and a glass of water.

items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: A slice of cake with dark blue icing and edible stars. The “Universe Edition”. Lola says to eat it slowly and look at the sky afterwards. Trust her.

items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: A brownie called “Captain's Calm”. Very soft, very chocolate, and very, very relaxing. Do not operate heavy machinery. Or yachts.

items.feld: Midnight Toastie with Cheese and Fig · wholesome
items.alt: From Lola's galley. Eat it yourself: energy +1.
items.neu: A midnight toastie with melted cheese and fig jam, cut into triangles, because triangles taste better. Everyone knows that.

items.alt: Vietnamese noodle soup with crab and tomato.
items.neu: Vietnamese noodle soup with crab, tomato and a red, slightly sour broth. A dish from a street stall in Hanoi, carried across the world in someone's memory.

items.alt: Caramelised pork belly with egg, served with rice.
items.neu: Pork belly braised in caramel and fish sauce until it falls apart, with eggs and rice. Families in Vietnam make it for the New Year and eat it for days.

items.alt: Petru: “Why is it in a bowl?”
items.neu: Rice, vegetables, beef and a fried egg in a hot stone bowl, mixed at the table. Petru looked at it for a long time and asked why it's in a bowl.

items.alt: Fresh rice paper rolls with prawns and herbs.
items.neu: Rice paper rolls with prawns, mint and lettuce, almost see-through. Light enough to eat on a hot deck. Dangerous with peanut sauce.

items.alt: The broth needs patience. Rosi knows ramen from her manga.
items.neu: A broth that simmered for hours, noodles, a soft egg and a slice of pork. Good ramen is patience you can drink.

items.alt: Too hot for a seasick fleet manager.
items.neu: Wok noodles with chilli oil and spring onions, hot enough to make your nose run. Not for the seasick. Not for the faint of heart either.

items.alt: Provençal fish stew with rouille.
items.neu: Provençal fish stew with saffron, rouille and toasted bread. The fishermen of Marseille made it from the fish they couldn't sell. Now it's the most expensive thing on the menu.

items.alt: Steamed buns with pork belly. Lola: “Fluffy clouds, Boss.”
items.neu: Soft steamed buns with glazed pork belly, cucumber and coriander. Fluffy as clouds. Gone in two bites.

items.alt: Fish under a potato crust. Petru: “Hm.” That means: another one.
items.neu: White fish and prawns under a golden crust of mashed potato. Someone in the village made it every Sunday for years. Nobody makes it quite like that anymore.

items.alt: Totò: “In Napoli, this is a crime.”
items.neu: Spaghetti with a long-simmered meat sauce. Totò says that in Naples this is a crime. He eats two plates anyway.

items.alt: Fried potatoes with sausage, onion, a fried egg and beetroot.
items.neu: Diced potatoes, sausage and onion fried in one pan, with a fried egg and beetroot. Scandinavian comfort food, best eaten after a cold watch.

items.alt: Norwegian fish soup with salmon, cream and dill.
items.neu: Norwegian fish soup with salmon, cream and dill. It tastes of a harbour in the rain and a kitchen that's warm.

items.alt: Smoked haddock, potatoes and milk, the Scottish way. The only thing Megan keeps down at sea.
items.neu: Cullen Skink: smoked haddock, potatoes and milk, the Scottish way. A fisherman's soup from a cold coast, gentle on the stomach.

items.alt: Bread is the hardest discipline.
items.neu: Fresh baguettes, crust that shatters, crumb that sighs. Bread is the hardest discipline. Everything else is just cooking.
